subject: history_social
passage: Today the word "Luddite" is applied to anyone who distrusts new technology, a usage implying that the original Luddites, English textile workers who smashed machinery between 1811 and 1816, were simply hostile to machines. The record of their actions suggests a narrower grievance. Many of the stocking frames they broke were not new inventions at all, having been in use for more than two centuries, and raiders often wrecked the frames of employers who paid below customary rates or produced cheap, poorly made goods while sparing those of employers who did not. What the Luddites opposed, in other words, was less machinery as such than the uses to which particular employers put it, a distinction their modern namesake has largely erased.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To show that the Luddites opposed only machines that had recently been invented
choices.B: To argue that the Luddites' resistance succeeded in raising textile workers' wages
choices.C: To contend that a familiar term misrepresents the motives of the group it is named for
choices.D: To explain how the Luddites organized and carried out their raids on textile employers

explanation.why: The text opens with the modern meaning of "Luddite," which implies the original Luddites "were simply hostile to machines." It then gives evidence (old machines, selective raids) of "a narrower grievance" and concludes that the modern usage has "largely erased" that distinction. The purpose is to correct what the term suggests about the group.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text stresses that many frames they broke had been in use for more than two centuries.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never says whether the raids changed wages; it discusses only what the Luddites objected to.
explanation.C: Correct. The author argues that the modern word wrongly implies a general hostility to machines that the Luddites' actions do not show.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Details about which frames were broken serve as evidence about motives; the text does not explain how raids were organized.
